en.headline: Customs seize 15kg suspected ketamine at airport, arrest Malaysian woman
en.dek: Officers found the drugs concealed in coffee powder packages in the checked luggage of a 28-year-old passenger who arrived from Paris via Taipei; the case remains under investigation.
body: Hong Kong Customs said on Sunday it had detected a drug trafficking case at Hong Kong International Airport involving an incoming passenger and seized about 15 kilograms of suspected ketamine with an estimated market value of HK$5.4 million.

A 28-year-old Malaysian woman arrived in Hong Kong from Paris, France, via Taipei. During customs clearance, officers found the suspected ketamine inside coffee powder packaging in her checked luggage. She was arrested immediately.

The case is still under investigation. Customs said it would continue to use intelligence analysis to combat drug trafficking and would select passengers from higher-risk areas for inspection under its risk-management approach.
Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. On conviction, the maximum penalty is a fine of HK$5 million and life imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關機場檢15公斤懷疑氯胺酮 拘28歲馬來西亞女
zh.dek: 關員在由巴黎經台北抵港的女子寄倉行李咖啡粉包裝內發現毒品，估計市值約540萬元，案件仍在調查。
body: 香港海關周日表示，在香港國際機場偵破一宗入境旅客販毒案件，檢獲約15公斤懷疑氯胺酮，估計市值約540萬元，並拘捕一名女子。
一名28歲馬來西亞籍女旅客由法國巴黎經台北飛抵本港。海關人員清關時，在其寄倉行李內的咖啡粉包裝中發現共約15公斤懷疑氯胺酮，隨即將她拘捕。
案件仍在調查中。海關表示會繼續根據情報分析加強打擊販運毒品活動，並會按風險管理原則重點揀選來自高風險地區的旅客作清關檢查。
根據《危險藥物條例》，販運危險藥物屬嚴重罪行，一經定罪，最高可被判罰款500萬元及終身監禁。
